1000514.etyen:
Borrowed from English Nancy (“female given name”). The deeper history of the English name is somewhat uncertain. It has long been used as a pet form of Ann, while historically it was also used as a diminutive of Middle English Annis, a form of Agnes. First attested in the 18th c.
Under the Ann analysis, the name belongs to the Anna name family, ultimately from Late Latin Anna (“female given name”), from Koine Greek Ἄννα (Ánna, “Anna”), from Biblical Hebrew חַנָּה (Ḥannāh, “Hannah; grace, favour”).

1005122.etyen:
PIE word
 *h₂éd
Compound of Ciss-dur (“C-sharp major”) + akkord (“chord”), literally “C-sharp-major chord”.
The first element Ciss-dur (“C-sharp major”) contains Ciss (“C-sharp”), the capitalized form of ciss, formed from c (“C”) and -iss (“sharp-note-forming suffix”); the suffix is from German -is (“sharp-note-forming suffix”), whose further origin is uncertain. The second part of Ciss-dur, dur (“major”), is via German Dur (“major”) from Middle High German bēdūre (“B-natural; hard B”), from Medieval Latin b durum (“hard B”). The adjective is from Latin dūrus (“hard”), from Proto-Italic *dūros
